keyAssumptions: ROSTER BASIS: CBRE's IN-PLACE PRO-FORMA for calendar year 2027 (page 9), which is what the $1,290,174 in-place NOI, the $204,109 recovery line, the $31,211 percentage rent and the $1,594,783 effective gross revenue all tie to. Where a suite has a 2027 step or a modeled renewal, the PSF here is the CY2027 blend; the site plan's current rate is stated in each tenant's rentSchedule.

The OM's In-Place Pro-Forma prints lease dates as month-year only with no day. Commencements are recorded as the FIRST day and expirations as the LAST day of the printed month — a stated convention, not a figure read off the document. Re-key exact days from the rent roll.

Four-way tie-out against the OM's printed totals: (a) roster SF sums to 113,652 = the stated GLA, with no vacancy (100% occupied); (b) base rents sum to $1,359,464 = the printed Total Tenant Revenue Occupied; (c) tenant recoveries sum to $204,107 vs the $204,109 printed (rounding); (d) $1,594,783 EGR - $304,610 OpEx = $1,290,173 vs the $1,290,174 NOI printed (rounding).

FOOTNOTE RECONSTRUCTION — IMPORTANT. The OM's page-9 footnote block extracts OUT OF ORDER, so the numbered markers had to be re-tied to tenants rather than read straight off. Every assignment used here is confirmed ARITHMETICALLY, not guessed: the four pending-renewal notes reproduce the exact CY2027 blended PSF for Omelet Cafe ($23.30 x 8mo + $24.50 x 4mo = $23.70), Sally Beauty ($21.78 x 3mo + $24.50 x 9mo = $23.82), Sport Clips ($21.78 x 8mo + $24.50 x 4mo = $22.69) and GameStop ($22.00 x 1mo + $24.50 x 11mo = $24.29); the 7%-over-$775,000 percentage rent ties to Kobe (the only tenant with percentage rent, and the only December 2031 expiry); the 12%-over-$583,333 note ties to Cato ($583,333 x 12% = $70,000, the natural breakpoint on Cato's $69,993 base rent); the May 2027 - April 2028 '6th lease year' kickout ties to Petsense (commenced April/May 2022); leaving the February 2027 - January 2028 $2M kickout with Bealls Outlet, whose fiscal year ends in January and whose $2M threshold is ~$86/SF on 23,275 SF. Spot-check these against the rent roll, but each one reproduces a printed figure exactly.

FOUR OF THE NINETEEN LEASES ARE ON PENDING, UNEXECUTED RENEWALS that CBRE has modeled (Omelet Cafe, Sally Beauty, Sport Clips, GameStop — all marked with an asterisk on the site plan). Their contractual leases expire in March 2027, August 2027 (x2) and January 2027. The site plan's own footnote says the expirations 'reflect pending lease extension.' The 100% occupancy headline and roughly $160,000 of CY2027 base rent depend on those four being signed.

TWO TENANTS ARE MODELED WITH ZERO EXPENSE REIMBURSEMENT: Cato ($69,993 base on 4,950 SF) and Bealls Outlet ($136,458 base on 23,275 SF). Together that is 25% of the GLA recovering nothing, which points to gross or heavily capped structures and is why the center recovers only $204,109 against $304,610 of operating expenses (a 67% recovery ratio). Verify both structures against the leases.

The CVS and AutoZone REA rows print an impossible date range in the OM (Start Jan-23, End Dec-21). Those dates are LEFT NULL here rather than carried into the library; both rows are marked NAP so they do not distort GLA, occupancy or rent-PSF math, and their $4,619 of combined CAM contribution remains inside the $204,109 recovery line.

THE OM'S '$15.07 PSF AVERAGE BASE RENT' HEADLINE (page 3) DOES NOT RECONCILE to its own rent roll. The page-9 roster rolls up to $11.96/SF ($1,359,464 / 113,652 SF), and CBRE's own page-10 cash flow shows a CY2027 weighted-average in-place rent of $11.92. The roster roll-up of $11.96 is recorded here; ask the broker what basis produces $15.07.
NO PRICE AND NO CAP RATE are quoted — unpriced marketing package. Value must be underwritten off the $1,290,174 in-place NOI.

TAXES ARE NOT REASSESSED. The $74,129 CY2027 tax line is the 2026 budget grown forward; the OM states expressly that reassessment is the investor's responsibility. At $0.65/SF the modeled tax line is strikingly low for a 113,652 SF Georgia community center — Effingham County will reassess on sale, and this is the largest single expense risk in the deal.
The OM does not print a year built, a renovation year, or any co-tenancy or exclusive-use clause. Left null rather than estimated.

redFlags.description: NEARLY 40% OF GLA ROLLS IN 2028 AND 66% IS ROLLED BY THE END OF 2029 (CBRE's own expiration schedule: 7,300 SF in 2027, 37,240 SF in 2028, 30,426 SF in 2029 — cumulative 65.96%). Goodwill (20,328 SF, March 2028), Dollar Tree (8,470 SF, July 2028) and Harbor Freight (20,976 SF, January 2029) all reach term inside three years with no disclosed renewal options. A '100% occupied, stabilized' asset with two-thirds of its area rolling in three years is a leasing project, not a coupon.

THE 100% OCCUPANCY HEADLINE RESTS PARTLY ON UNSIGNED PAPER. Four leases — Omelet Cafe, Sally Beauty, Sport Clips and GameStop — expire between January and August 2027 with no remaining contractual options, and their post-2027 terms are renewals CBRE has MODELED, not executed. Sally Beauty's contractual expiry is March 2027, likely before a closing would complete. Confirm each renewal in writing before crediting the term.

TWO SALES KICKOUTS ARE LIVE INSIDE THE FIRST TWO YEARS AND NEITHER CAN BE ASSESSED. Bealls Outlet, the largest tenant at 20.5% of GLA, has a one-time kickout if February 2027 - January 2028 sales are under $2,000,000; Petsense has a one-time kickout after its 6th lease year (May 2027 - April 2028) if sales do not exceed $700,000. NO SALES ARE DISCLOSED FOR EITHER TENANT, so there is no way to judge whether either is at risk. Together they are 28,807 SF and $220,475 of base rent — 17% of the center's rent. Get the sales before bidding.

25% of the GLA recovers nothing. Bealls Outlet (23,275 SF) and Cato (4,950 SF) are both modeled with $0 expense reimbursement, which is why the center recovers only $204,109 against $304,610 of operating expenses — a 67% recovery ratio that is weak for a center marketed as NNN. Every dollar of expense growth on those two suites, including a post-sale tax reassessment, falls to ownership.

The modeled real-estate tax line is $74,129, just $0.65/SF on a 113,652 SF center — implausibly low for a Georgia community center at a major intersection, and expressly NOT reassessed. A reassessment to a market purchase price could move this line materially, and 25% of the GLA cannot recover any of it.

Cato is a watch item: $110 PSF of sales at a 13% occupancy cost (OM-stated), expiring January 2028, with sales BELOW its $583,333 percentage-rent breakpoint so it generates no overage. Shoe Show is worse on health — a 14% occupancy cost on $139 PSF — and expires October 2027, the very first roll.
GameStop's modeled renewal is only TWO YEARS, versus five for the other three pending renewals — a signal about that tenant's own commitment in a business that is closing stores nationally.

SALES ARE DISCLOSED FOR ONLY FOUR OF NINETEEN TENANTS (Kobe, Cato, Hibbett, Shoe Show). The three largest tenants by area — Bealls Outlet, Harbor Freight and Goodwill, 57% of GLA between them — have no productivity data at all, and two of the four disclosed tenants are the weakest performers.
Goodwill's lease is with a regional Goodwill affiliate, not a national credit, and no guaranty is disclosed — on 17.9% of GLA and the center's largest single base rent.

Strong and fast-growing trade area: 3-mile average household income of $112,238 (median $93,066) and a 5-mile population up 64% since 2010, growing 3.47% annually. deals.notes: Fort Howard Square is a 113,652 SF, 100% leased community center on 12.7 acres at the South Columbia Avenue / Fort Howard Road intersection (34,800 VPD) in Rincon, Georgia, a fast-growing Savannah suburb, offered unpriced by CBRE within the Project Evergreen portfolio. It is the dominant center in its trade area — #1 of four within five miles by foot traffic with 71% more visits than the runner-up, 1.7 million annual visits, and the next comparable retail concentration 10+ miles away — anchored by Bealls Outlet, Harbor Freight, Goodwill and Dollar Tree and drawing cross-shopping from a Walmart Supercenter, Lowe's and Kroger Marketplace at the same corner. In-place CY2027 NOI is $1,290,174 on $1,594,783 of effective gross revenue against $304,610 of operating expenses, at a roster-computed $11.96/SF weighted-average base rent against CBRE's $16.17/SF modeled market rent — the 24%-below-market spread the OM headlines. The trade area is the strongest in this portfolio group: $112,238 3-mile average household income, a 5-mile population up 64% since 2010 and still growing 3.47% a year, with roughly 1,000 residential units built or proposed within two miles. The catch is that a center marketed as stabilized is really a three-year leasing project: nearly 40% of GLA rolls in 2028 and 66% is rolled by the end of 2029, none of it with disclosed options, and the 100% occupancy figure itself depends on four renewals — Omelet Cafe, Sally Beauty, Sport Clips and GameStop — that CBRE has modeled but the OM does not state as executed. Two live sales kickouts sit inside the first two years, on Bealls Outlet (the largest tenant, if February 2027 to January 2028 sales miss $2 million) and Petsense (if 6th-lease-year sales miss $700,000), together covering 17% of base rent, and no sales are disclosed for either. Add 25% of the GLA recovering zero expenses and a $0.65/SF unreassessed tax line, and the expense side carries real downside. The thesis is sound — a dominant, below-market center in a booming Savannah suburb — but it should be priced as a value-add re-leasing story with unquantified kickout risk, not as stabilized income.
